content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper introduces a VAE-based time series pattern discovery approach. The main technical contribution is using a Binary Concrete distribution in the VAE structure. In the experiment, the approach only compared with MP-snippet, which is not a motif discovery approach in human activity recognition and one of the synthesis data in the UCR time series archive. The authors claimed that the approach is more efficient than the current existing motif discovery algorithm while the algorithm can find meaningful patterns under MDL.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength: 
1. Pattern Discovery is an important task

Weakness

1. The authors largely ignore a large body of pattern discovery works.

2. Lacking novelty and intuition: The authors haven't conducted any ablation tests. It is very not convincing why the proposed VAE is better. In addition, the new proposed VAE is merely changing the prior, it is not clear why its works. 

3. The experiment is poorly designed. For example, authors said it compared with MP-snippet. It is even not a motif discovery approach. More detailed in the summary of the review.

Detailed Comments needs to address by authors: Please see the summary of review
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The manuscript lacks an explanation of the intuition of the proposed work. The proposed technique is incremental since it is entirely designed on top of classical VAE. In addition, the work largely ignores existing works and does not share the source code. The experiment design is poor and is not convincing.
content.summary_of_the_review:
This paper introduces a VAE-based time series pattern discovery approach or motif discovery approach named T2P. However, the technical contribution is very low and the paper largely ignores a large body of pattern discovery research. The comparison experiment is poorly designed. Overall, this paper is not ready for publishing. Here are the detailed comments: 

1. First of all, the authors ignore a large body of high-citation classical pattern discovery approaches as well as recent approaches. Just named a few here [1-4]. Missing this article significantly affects the claims in this paper. 

    For example, the authors claim T2P is much more efficient than MP. However, [2][4] has linear or close to linear time complexity, [1][3] 
    could have more efficient motif discovery performance when the subsequence length is small. Moreover, there is an anytime version 
    algorithm [5] (e.g. algorithm could stop anytime and return the pattern discovery result). None of them are mentioned and compared. As 
    a result, the claim becomes very unconvincing.

2. The method here heavily relies on the VAE structure by merely changing the prior and seems incremental. However, the intuition behind the such change is unclear. The information provided in the article is insufficient to justify the change. Moreover, an ablation study is not conducted in this paper (i.e. compared with other VAE, how is the performance). Therefore, the novelty is low, intuition is very unclear, and the claims are not justified.

3. Why compared with an MP-snippet? It is even not a motif discovery approach, but rather a time series summarization approach. Note that time series summarization is only a downstream task for motif discovery. A motif discovered should have the ability to explain events and may use to build a classifier to classify time series in a variety of types of time series (see the experiment in the [1-4]). 


4. Lacking experiment setting detailed. For example, what is the setting for the proposed VAE? What is the input of VAE (e.g. are you using a sliding window to feed the samples)? What is the length of the pattern and time series? How many subsequences do you feed into VAE? What algorithm did you use to compress the time series?  


5. From Fig. 6, I personally think the discovered patterns do not have sufficient power to summarize the data (since every sample shown seems a mixture of classes. In addition, for the time series dataset setting [1], why not use some new techniques specially designed for it such as [6]?


6. Finally, a VAE model needs to be trained to do the pattern discovery. Therefore, how do you evaluate the running time? It is never shown in the article. Have you used GPU? Since all the approaches mentioned here do not run on GPU, it is unfair to evaluate speed in different hardware situations. To make a fair comparison, I suggest you report and compare the execution time of the GPU version motif discovery approach such as [7], which is obviously not the one reported in the figure.



[1] Mueen A, Keogh E, Zhu Q, Cash S, Westover B. Exact discovery of time series motifs. InProceedings of the 2009 SIAM international conference on data mining 2009 Apr 30 (pp. 473-484). Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics.

[2] Chiu B, Keogh E, Lonardi S. Probabilistic discovery of time series motifs. InProceedings of the ninth ACM SIGKDD international conference on Knowledge discovery and data mining 2003 Aug 24 (pp. 493-498).

[3] Li Y, Leong HU, Yiu ML, Gong Z. Quick-motif: An efficient and scalable framework for exact motif discovery. In2015 IEEE 31st International Conference on Data Engineering 2015 Apr 13 (pp. 579-590). IEEE.

[4] Gao Y, Lin J. HIME: discovering variable-length motifs in large-scale time series. Knowledge and Information Systems. 2019 Oct;61(1):513-42.

[5] Yeh CC, Zhu Y, Ulanova L, Begum N, Ding Y, Dau HA, Silva DF, Mueen A, Keogh E. Matrix profile I: all pairs similarity joins for time series: a unifying view that includes motifs, discords and shapelets. In2016 IEEE 16th international conference on data mining (ICDM) 2016 Dec 12 (pp. 1317-1322). Ieee.

[6] Kamgar K, Gharghabi S, Keogh E. Matrix profile XV: Exploiting time series consensus motifs to find structure in time series sets. In2019 IEEE International Conference on Data Mining (ICDM) 2019 Nov 8 (pp. 1156-1161). IEEE.

content.summary_of_the_paper:
Considering the potential issues of time series pattern search in existing studies, in this paper, the author(s) proposed a variational auto-encoder (VAE)-based probabilistic time-to-pattern mining algorithms to encode representative statistical variational patterns in the time series. Empirical experiments showed the advantage of the proposed algorithm.

---
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
In my opinion, the Weaknesses and strengths of this paper are as follows:

### Strength:


1. The proposed algorithm does not depend on any concrete distance function/metric and can detect potential patterns.

2. The proposed algorithm is scalable and efficient (the running time is almost constant as the size of the data increases).

---

### Weaknesses:

1. The details of empirical experiments are not so sufficient/clear.

2. The novelty of this proposed algorithm seems limited.

For more details, please see the section "Clarity, Quality, Novelty And Reproducibility" below.

---
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
This paper is generally well written; however, I have the following comments/questions. I look forward to the response from the author(s). Thanks.

---

### Clarity:

1. Some descriptions in this paper are not so clear. For example,

(1) On Page 2, Line 1, it said that "...which might also not be the most informative for some applications.". Could the author(s) please give one or two specific examples of some of these applications?

(2) On Page 2, Paragraph 2, the last sentence, "... to reduce the search space, but the compression is lossy and may cause important patterns to be undetected." The compression is lossy, the VAE used in this paper is also a kind of compression, does not have a loss issue?

---

2. Some experimental details are not clear. For instance, how many epochs were used, what was the learning rate, and whether regularization was used when performing the optimization

And, in this paper, the author(s) performed empirical experiments, but I am not sure the empirical description/experiments would be enough to reproduce because no code of this paper seems to be provided (I only noticed the pseudo-code description of the proposed algorithm).

---

### Novelty

I think the novelty of this proposed algorithm in this paper is limited. 

1. The idea of this paper seems to be similar to concrete auto-encoders [1]. The only difference is that this paper is for the latent space, and the concrete auto-encoder is for the original feature space, While this paper did not mention [1].

2. The difference with [2] is mainly that "bin" in [2] is replaced with "distribution" in VAE, right?


[1] Balın MF, Abid A, Zou J. Concrete autoencoders: Differentiable feature selection and reconstruction. In International conference on machine learning 2019 May 24 (pp. 444-453). PMLR.

[2] Noering FK, Schroeder Y, Jonas K, Klawonn F. Pattern discovery in time series using autoencoder in comparison to nonlearning approaches. Integrated Computer-Aided Engineering. 2021 Jan 1;28(3):237-56.

---

In addition, some other tiny issues/typos

(1) Section 2.2 has too much content, VAE is already a standard model, there is no need to use so much content in the main text to describe, if possible, please simplify the section, and put the extra content in the Supplementary Materials.

(2) In general, the first time an abbreviation appears, it needs to go with the full name. Then, if the abbreviation is followed, the full name does not need to appear again. However, time-to-pattern (T2P) appears many times in this paper.

(3) The definition of mathematical notations, repeat many times. For example, $\mathbf{x}$ in the 3rd paragraph of Section 2.1 and the first paragraph of Section 3.1. And mathematical formulas sometimes end with punctuation, sometimes they don't.

(4) The format of the references is quite inconsistent. Please check carefully and correct it.

---
content.summary_of_the_review: Time series pattern mining is one of the important problems in data mining. The work in this paper is interesting; However, there are many unclear aspects in the description (including experimental details) of this paper, and the innovation also needs to be further discussed.

content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.

content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes a VAE-based information theoretic sequence mining. The basic idea is to embed a sequence to a space of a continuous relaxed Bernoulli distribution, from which representative sequences are reconstructed. The empirical results suggest that the proposed method can be effective for discovering patterns.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:

- Combining VAE and pattern mining is an interesting approach.
- Illustrative examples illustrate the proposed method actually can find representative patterns.    

Weaknesses:

- The technical description is quite similar to Kirschbaum et al. 2019. Although the authors cite it in Sec3.2, I think similarity should have been clarified more explicitly in Sec3.3. Although the input is a video sequence in Kirschbaum et al. 2019, the definition of the VAE model is almost same as the proposed method. The current manuscript can mislead readers that the model described in Sec3.3 is the authors novelty. Because of this overlap, I think technical novelty is not outstanding. 

- I felt difficulty to understand the detailed procedure of the proposed method, partially because the paper contains many ambiguous descriptions and typos such as 
  - A nonitalic x is first defined as a length n time-series in which a italic x is a scalar value at a time point, but in Sec3.3, a italic x is seemingly a sequence.
  - z is first defined a binary variable, but in (2) it becomes continuous value (I think the relaxed value should be a different symbol).
  - \alpha_1 and \alpha_2 suddenly appear before (2), but detail is not explained. In (3), only alpha = \alpha_2/\alpha_1 is used (although in the main text it is written as \alpha^2/alpha^1, I guess it should be \alpha_1/\alpha_2). Then, why alpha_1 and alpha_2 are required separately?
  - Binary Concrete distribution is not clearly described. In Sec3.3, related equations (2), (3) and (5) are suddenly defined without clarifying the underlying basic idea. For these equations, the authors directly used equations of Maddison et al., 2016 and Kirschbaum et al. 2019. It should have stated more clearly, though they are cited in Sec.3.2.
  - In (4), the sign of KL should be '+'.
  - I guess (5) is g_a,lambda_1(Y|x), but it is not clearly written, and I am first confused about what it represents. A further confusion is caused by that, in (5), x has different meaning from other texts (in (5), x corresponds to 'Y') and further, alpha in this equation would be different from alpha in (3). 
  - B_KL is not defined. What is it?
  - In the end, how representative sequences (called 'learned pattern' in the paper) are selected? From learned z?
  - What is the index 'i' of the Fig4? It does not appear inside the product.
  - In Fig4, f_\theta would be the decoder and \alpha(x;\phi) would be the encoder, but it is not described in the main text.
  - I was confused whether the input of the encoder is the full sequence or a subseqeunce. For example, in Fig8, the input seems the full sequence because 'x' (without '+') is conditioned on q, but in the Algorithm1, x is a subsequence. 
  - Throughout the paper, it is difficult to tell a vector and a scalar. For example, I currently guess z represents both of them depending on context.

- The authors recommend a specific setting of hyper-parameters (\beta, \lambda, a, and B). Although the authors claim the setting is generally effective, its justification is not clear. For example, the authors mentioned that the proposed method does not work with \beta_MSE = 1, but works well with \beta_MSE = 0.8. No rationale of this claim is provided, by which I am not convinced.

- The authors repeatedly refer Hebb (2005) and clam the proposed method is inspired by 'neuronal ensemble'. However, I feel the discussion is somewhat vague, and more detailed justification is desired. In the beginning of Sec3.1, the authors define the informative pattern through conditional independence. For me, it is unclear how the current formulation can achieve it.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
Clarity: As I describe above, technical description of the paper is not fully clear.

Quality: Technical quality is ok.

Novelty: Technical novelty with respect to the VAE model is somewhat weak because of the prior work (Kirschbaum et al. 2019). Although the target data is different (video and time-series), the model definition (VAE with Binary Concrete distribution) is quite similar.

Reproducibility: OK.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper focuses on an interesting approach, but technical novelty is somewhat limited because of the large overlap with mainly (Kirschbaum et al. 2019). Low readability also degrades reliability of the paper.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The manuscript proposes a method of pattern discovery in time series data named time-to-pattern (T2P). Patterns found by T2P are based on information-theoretic criteria and its goal is to identify the set of patterns that best summarizes the time series. T2P uses a variational autoencoder (VAE) that extends the implementation of neuronal assemblies and determines an embedding space from which the optimal set of patterns is obtained. T2P does not rely on any distance function and the authors claim it outperforms other state-of-the-art approaches.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
- the motivation for the work is clear and well-written.
- the authors place T2P in the context of other approaches to mine patterns in time series
- the use of the VAE is well-motivated. The main text and appendix provide good descriptions of VAEs and how the loss is implemented in T2P.

Weaknesses
- The authors’ claim that T2P has a lower computational complexity than other state-of-the-art pattern mining approaches is not discussed in detail. The introduction presents the complexity of several methods but this is not followed up by an analysis of the complexity of T2P.
- T2P is proposed in a field with a vast array of methods and approaches. Yet, the authors only compare their proposed method to MP-Snippets (Imani, et al. 2018). This, in my opinion, is the main drawback of this work. There are big and important claims about the proposed method but these are not substantiated by comparing it to other approaches. Why not compare T2P, for example, to the methods listed in the Introduction? Here I suggest several other comparison partners, some of which can essentially be used as baselines as they focus on extracting shapelets from time series, i.e.,  subsequences in time series that are representative of a group. In particular [4] (and its current optimized variations of the original algorithm) should be included as a comparison partner since it challenges the premise of this paper on how Euclidean distances are detrimental for this task:
[1] Ye, Lexiang, and Eamonn Keogh. "Time series shapelets: a new primitive for data mining." Proceedings of the 15th ACM SIGKDD international conference on Knowledge discovery and data mining. 2009.
[2] Grabocka, Josif, et al. "Learning time-series shapelets." Proceedings of the 20th ACM SIGKDD international conference on Knowledge discovery and data mining. 2014.
[3] Bock, Christian, et al. "Association mapping in biomedical time series via statistically significant shapelet mining." Bioinformatics 34.13 (2018): i438-i446.
[4] Mueen, Abdullah, et al. "The fastest similarity search algorithm for time series subsequences under Euclidean distance. url: www cs unm edu/∼ mueen." FastestSimilaritySearch html (Accessed 24 May 2016) (2015).
- It is unclear how T2P the analysis about “Scalability” is performed. What programming language did the authors use? The supplementary material does not contain the code. Are the 2 code bases (T2P vs. MP-Snippets comparable)? I also recommend the authors to perform a more exhaustive analysis of the scalability of the method. Only 3 time points is not sufficient in my opinion.
- The model is heavily parameterized but it is not clear to me from reading section 3.4 how all these parameters are optimized. The authors should clearly state how the data is partitioned in order to train the model, learn its parameters and to provide a measure of how the loss is reduced for different sets of hyperparameters. The choice of parameters in Section 3.3 has an ad-hoc flavor in my opinion.
- I recommend the authors to better develop sections 5.2 and 5.3 in order to make a more convincing case about the use of T2P. Currently, the results presented there (Fig. 5. And 6) show examples of time series snippets discovered by MP-Snippets and these are contrasted to the patterns found by T2P. Visually, there seem to be no differences in the sets of patterns reported by MP-Snippets and T2P. Perhaps this can be turned into a table in which the patterns are quantified?
- Moreover, it seems that the patterns reported by T2P need an additional level of post-processing or summarization. The T2P patterns shown in Fig. 5 and 6 seem almost identical to each other.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper has a clear motivation and is well-written. The ideas presented are interesting but not well developed in my opinion. No code was shared, thus it is hard to assess the reproducibility of the proposed method.
content.summary_of_the_review: The authors present a solid case on the need of alternative methods for pattern mining in time series. The proposed method, T2P, draws from interesting ideas. Its novelty is hampered by (i) a lack of clarity on how the parameters of the model are learned/optimized, and (ii) no substantive comparison against other state-of-the-art  algorithms for pattern matching in time series (most of which, by the way, are mentioned in the Introduction)
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
